decisionMemo.businessProblem: A safety/quality incident hit and demand softened; the owner wants a marketing relaunch, but the product is still unsafe.

rootCauseDiagnosis.description: Absence of quality control process or quality assurance checkpoints
rootCauseDiagnosis.mechanismDescription: Without QA checkpoints, defects reach customers. Each complaint damages reputation and reduces repeat business.
alternativeExplanations: Quality standard may be poorly communicated to team
Team may lack skills to meet quality standard
missingEvidenceFor: What specifically is wrong with quality (consistency, defect rate, etc)
Root cause of quality issues (skills, materials, process)

criticalConstraints.description: Quality control processes not documented; team quality assurance capability limited

intervention.title: Implement complaint tracking and customer outreach
intervention.objective: Capture complaint data to identify patterns and immediately contact affected customers
intervention.rationale: Shows customers concerns are taken seriously; generates data for root cause analysis
intervention.whyThisNow: Immediate action to rebuild trust and prevent repeat customer loss

steps.title: Create complaint log template
steps.description: Record what went wrong, customer name, order details, resolution offered
steps.successCriteria: Template reviewed and approved by team

steps.title: Implement follow-up protocol
steps.description: All complaints receive same-day acknowledgment and manager review
steps.successCriteria: Complaints reviewed daily, customers contacted within 24 hours

steps.title: Analyze complaint patterns monthly
steps.description: Group complaints by cause, identify most common issue, propose countermeasure
steps.successCriteria: Monthly pattern report generated, top 3 issues identified

failureRisks: Complaint tracking abandoned after initial month
Follow-up feels insincere without real resolution
intervention.fallbackPlan: Use complaints to justify investment in full QA program or third-party quality auditing

recommendedInterventions.sequencingReason: Quick implementation builds momentum and shows progress

intervention.title: Implement quality checkpoints before customer delivery
intervention.objective: Establish QA checkpoints to prevent defect shipment and catch issues early
intervention.rationale: Reduces complaint rate by catching issues before customer, improves team quality awareness
intervention.whyThisNow: Foundational quality practice that can begin immediately without capital

steps.title: Define quality standard and checklist
steps.description: Based on complaint patterns, define what 'good quality' means and create inspection checklist
steps.successCriteria: Checklist covers 80% of historical complaint causes

steps.title: Assign quality checkpoint responsibility
steps.description: Designate team member or create rotation for pre-shipment quality check
steps.successCriteria: Team trained on checklist, ownership clear

steps.title: Track defects caught vs. released
steps.description: For 4 weeks, log defects caught at checkpoint vs shipped (escaped) defects
steps.successCriteria: >85% of defects caught at checkpoint, escaped defect rate <5%

failureRisks: Checklist too complex, team skips steps
QA checker lacks authority to stop shipment
No time allocated for quality check
intervention.fallbackPlan: Simplify checklist to 3 critical items only, assign most experienced team member as QA owner

recommendedInterventions.sequencingReason: Critical revenue urgency requires immediate stabilization

scenarios.name: Aggressive Recovery (Best Case)
scenarios.description: Execute all interventions in optimal sequence with full team commitment
assumptions: Team capacity fully available (no other initiatives)
Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)
scenarios.description: Execute top 3 prioritized interventions sequentially, measure, then decide on next wave
assumptions: Top 3 interventions address critical path to revenue recovery
Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Measurable improvement in 60 days, foundation for growth set
risks: Slower overall recovery than aggressive path
Competitors may advance while we execute gradually

scenarios.name: Defensive Hold (Minimal Risk)
scenarios.description: Execute containment interventions only to stabilize immediate crisis
assumptions: Focus on preserving cash and customer base
External investment or M&A may be needed for growth
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Stabilize revenue decline, buy time for external support
risks: Does not address root causes; temporary relief only
Competitors gain market share during hold period
Team morale declines with no visible improvement
